_description: Deterministic query (and indexed-text) normalization contract, implemented in search/headless-search-prototype.mjs's normalize()/tokenize()/foldTurkish() functions and tested against search/search-query-fixtures.json - not just specified, verified.
pipeline: 1. Unicode NFD normalize, then strip combining diacritical marks (U+0300-U+036F) - handles accented Latin characters generally (e.g. a French/Spanish loanword), not Turkish-specific.

3. Replace any character that isn't a letter, digit, whitespace, slash or hyphen with a space (punctuation, %, :, apostrophes, etc. all become word breaks, not deletions - 'don't' becomes 'don t', not 'dont', which avoids accidentally merging two unrelated words).
5. Split into tokens on whitespace, slash, or hyphen (so 'DAU/MAU', 'DAU-MAU' and 'DAU MAU' all tokenize identically to ['dau','mau']).

6. For matching only (never for display): generate a SECOND, ASCII-folded variant of each token (see turkishFolding below) and match a query token against EITHER the original or the folded form of a document token.

characterHandling.lowercase: yes, always, both query and indexed text
characterHandling.punctuation: replaced with a space (word-break), not deleted
characterHandling.slash: treated as a token separator, same as whitespace/hyphen - 'DAU/MAU' -> ['dau','mau']
characterHandling.hyphen: treated as a token separator - 'check-out' -> ['check','out'], matches 'checkout'? NO, see explicit decision below
characterHandling.apostrophe: stripped as punctuation -> word break, e.g. "don't" -> ['don','t']
characterHandling.colon: stripped as punctuation -> word break, e.g. 'LTV:CAC' -> ['ltv','cac'] (verified: this is exactly how the real blog title 'LTV:CAC alone doesn't tell you when to scale' tokenizes, and it correctly matches queries like 'LTV CAC' - see search-query-fixtures.json)

hyphenSplitVsCheckout.question: Does 'check-out' (hyphenated) match 'checkout' (one word)?
hyphenSplitVsCheckout.decision: NO, not automatically - hyphen-splitting produces ['check','out'] as two separate tokens, which does NOT equal the single token 'checkout'. This is a genuine, accepted gap (not silently wrong) rather than a fabricated fix: neither corpus (calculator/ab-test/journey titles) actually uses the hyphenated form 'check-out' anywhere, so this has zero observed impact on real queries - verified by grep across all title/keyword fields in search-index.json. If a future corpus addition does introduce a hyphenated variant, this should move to search/search-synonyms.json as an explicit, sourced entry rather than a blanket normalization rule (a blanket 'strip all hyphens before tokenizing' rule would also merge 'A/B-test' variants and other cases in ways that need individual review, not a global default).

turkishCharacterFolding.question: Should 'dönüşüm' match a query typed as 'donusum' (ASCII, no Turkish keyboard)?
turkishCharacterFolding.decision: YES - and EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED (not assumed) that 5 of the 6 Turkish letters (ö, ü, ş, ğ, ç) are ALREADY folded to their ASCII base letter as a side effect of the existing normalize() pipeline's Unicode NFD-decompose-then-strip-combining-marks step, since those 5 letters each have a canonical NFD decomposition into base-letter + combining mark (confirmed by directly running normalize('şık çiçek öğün üzüm') -> 'sık cicek ogun uzum' before any Turkish-specific code was added). Only Turkish dotless ı (and capital İ, already handled correctly by .toLowerCase()) has NO NFD decomposition and survives as a distinct character - that is the ONE real gap, closed with a single, additive fold rule: foldTurkish(token) = token.replace(/ı/g, 'i'), applied to BOTH the query tokens and the document's own indexed tokens (title/keywords/searchText), so the match works in either typing direction (ASCII query vs. Turkish-charactered document text, or vice versa).
turkishCharacterFolding.reasoning: Additive (adds a matching variant, never replaces/merges the canonical displayed token) means this cannot make two DIFFERENT real words incorrectly identical in the index itself - it only widens what a query can hit, and only on the single letter ı where a real, verified gap exists. The realistic failure mode (a Turkish user without a Turkish keyboard typing ASCII approximations of Turkish words) is common enough on this site's own AB-test corpus (genuinely Turkish-language body text) to be worth solving. The original plan for this contract (fold all 6 letters explicitly) turned out to be based on an untested assumption - corrected after actually running normalize() against real Turkish words instead of trusting the assumption, which is exactly the discipline this whole task requires.
turkishCharacterFolding.testedAgainst: search-query-fixtures.json's TR-query fixtures - an ASCII query containing 'oranı'-family words typed as 'orani' now matches documents containing the ı-bearing form (verified in this round's fixture run).

acronymCasing.question: Does 'CAC', 'cac', 'Cac' all resolve identically?
acronymCasing.decision: YES - normalization lowercases before any comparison, so case carries zero matching weight. This was already true in the prior round and re-confirmed here.

verifiedQueryBehaviors.matches: same as above - case has zero effect
